subject: Separate SPDE models for two regions

messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Separate SPDE models for two regions
parts:
Dear INLA experts,


I want to develop two SPDE models for two non-overlapping regions, one for each region. I want their results to be comparable, so I aim to reduce the impact of different mesh resolutions. 


The data for both regions have the same spatial resolution, but one region is more sparsely sampled, and the total areas of the two regions are different. 


If I set the same max.edge, offset, and cutoff for both meshes, will that make their results more comparable? Also, should the mesh be built based on the number of observed data points, I.e., less nodes for the region that is more sparsely sampled?


Thanks,

Ruby

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Separate SPDE models for two regions
parts:
Hi,

the meshes should have sufficient resolution for the spatial
variability structure of the latent fields. This is not necessarily
related to the distance between observations, so using the same
max.edge for both regions is probably a good idea.

Finn
